lessonRef.title: Unit assessment: survey, experiment, and observational study design

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Unit assessment. Work alone, show your steps, and check your work before you finish.

items.prompt: A random sample of 400 people gives a sample proportion of 55%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±5%, giving 50% to 60%
±55%, giving 0% to 110%
±10%, giving 45% to 65%

items.prompt: In 100 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 5 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 5% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 5% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 88 and standard deviation 5. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 73 and 103?
choices: about 95%
about 68%
about 50%
about 99.7%

items.prompt: A researcher runs a randomised controlled experiment with participants randomly assigned to treatments. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.

items.prompt: A random sample of 100 people gives a sample proportion of 37%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±1%, giving 36% to 38%

items.prompt: In 100 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 1 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 1% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.

The simulation proves that there is no difference.

items.prompt: A researcher runs a sample survey with randomly selected participants. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.

items.prompt: In 500 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 8 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 1.6% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 1.6% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
